newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi judge delays tobacco trial to July 7.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi judge delays tobacco trial to July 7.

text.p: A Mississippi judge on Thursday ordered the trial date in the state's landmark case against the tobacco industry to be delayed until July 7.

A day after tobacco lawyers argued at a three-hour hearing that a June 2 start would not give them enough time, Jackson County Chancery Judge William Myers decided to push the proceedings back by a little more than a month.
Mississippi is suing the industry to recoup about $1.0 billion in Medicaid funds spent treating poor people for smoking-related illnesses since the mid-1960s.
"Thirty days is not enough, but it's a great start," said tobacco industry attorney Joe Colingo, who did not rule out asking for more time as the new trial date approaches.
"It's going to be a great help. It's going to relieve a lot of the pressure from trying to do something that was impossible," he added.

Attorneys for Mississippi, who had argued against delaying the trial, also welcomed the order, saying it increased the chance that internal documents from the Liggett Group, which could prove damaging for the defendants, would be included as evidence.

"Now we have a breathing room of 30 days to allow us time to have the issue of the Liggett documents resolved so we can use the documents at the trial," said Charles Mikhail, a private attorney working for the state.
Liggett is unit of Brooke Group Ltd.
State Attorney General Mike Moore asked Myers to review the documents during Wednesday's hearing, but the judge did not indicate whether he would comply with the request.
Myers also limited each side to a maximum of 40 expert witnesses for the trial.
